title: Rival Teams
statement: A summer camp has campers numbered 0 to campers - 1 and a list of rivalries, each a pair [a, b] of campers who must not sleep in the same cabin. There are exactly two cabins and every camper must be placed in one of them. Return true if the campers can be split between the two cabins so that no rivalry pair shares a cabin, otherwise false. A camper with no rivalries may go in either cabin, and the same pair may be listed more than once.
constraints: Each rivalry is [a, b] with 0 <= a, b < campers and a != b

examples.explanation: Put campers 0 and 2 in one cabin and 1 and 3 in the other; every rivalry crosses between the cabins.
Any two of three mutual rivals would have to share a cabin, so no split exists.

hints.content: Treat campers as nodes and rivalries as edges. Every edge must join two different cabins.
Once you place one camper, each of their rivals is forced into the other cabin, and their rivals' rivals back into the first.
Different groups of connected campers are independent, so start a new search from every camper you have not placed yet.
Run a breadth-first search from an unplaced camper: give the start cabin 0, and give every newly found rival the opposite cabin of the camper who found them.
If you meet a rival who already holds the same cabin as the current camper, the groups contain an odd cycle and the answer is false. If every search finishes without a clash, return true.

testCases.explanation: An even cycle can be split.
A single camper with no rivalries.
The second group of rivals is a triangle even though the first is fine.
Repeated pairs and separate groups are fine.
A seven-camper loop is an odd cycle.
A path with one chord that closes the triangle 0, 2, 1.
A large random two-cabin split: only even-odd rivalries.
A long path plus a separate triangle: false.

solutions.title: Try cabins camper by camper and backtrack
solutions.intuition: Place campers one at a time into cabin 0 or 1 and back up whenever a rivalry with an earlier camper is violated.
solutions.approach: Keep a cabin array. Advance camper by camper, trying cabin 0 then cabin 1, rejecting an option that matches a rival with a smaller number. When both options fail, reset this camper and step back to the previous one. Reaching the end means a split exists; stepping back past camper 0 means none does.
solutions.pseudocode:
cabin = [-1] * campers; camper = 0
while 0 <= camper < campers:
  cabin[camper] += 1
  if cabin[camper] > 1: cabin[camper] = -1; camper -= 1
  elif no earlier rival shares cabin[camper]: camper += 1
return camper == campers
solutions.timeComplexity: O(2^campers) worst case, because a camper placed freely early can force many retries
commonMistakes: Checking rivals with a larger number, who have not been placed yet.
Forgetting to reset a camper's cabin to unplaced before stepping back.
solutions.interviewExplanation: This is an exhaustive search with pruning: it tries both cabins for each camper and only discards a branch when it contradicts a rival already placed. It is correct, but a camper with no earlier rival is placed freely, and a later conflict can force it to retry the other cabin exponentially often. A breadth-first search avoids the guessing entirely because each placement is forced.

steps.title: Place campers in order
steps.content: For the four-camper loop, camper 0 takes cabin 0, camper 1 takes cabin 1 and camper 2 must take cabin 0.

steps.title: Finish or back up
steps.content: Camper 3 takes cabin 1. All four are placed, so the answer is true. On the triangle, camper 2 clashes in both cabins, so the search backs up past camper 0 and returns false.

solutions.title: Breadth-first two-colouring
solutions.intuition: A rival of a camper is forced into the opposite cabin, so each connected group has at most one valid colouring and BFS finds it.
solutions.approach: Build adjacency lists. For every unplaced camper, set cabin 0 and run BFS: an unplaced rival gets the opposite cabin and joins the queue; a rival already in the same cabin proves an odd cycle and returns false. Return true when all groups finish.
solutions.pseudocode:
build adjacency
cabin = [-1]*n
for start: if cabin[start] == -1: cabin[start] = 0; queue = [start]
  while queue: u = pop
    for v in adj[u]: if cabin[v] == -1: cabin[v] = 1 - cabin[u]; push v
                     elif cabin[v] == cabin[u]: return false
return true
solutions.spaceComplexity: O(campers + rivalries) for the adjacency lists, the cabin array and the queue (every camper is queued at most once)
commonMistakes: Starting only from camper 0 and ignoring disconnected groups.
Marking campers as visited without storing their cabin, so the same-cabin clash is never detected.
Treating a repeated rivalry pair as a conflict.
solutions.interviewExplanation: A graph can be split into two cabins exactly when it is bipartite, meaning it has no odd cycle. Breadth-first search colours each connected group from a start camper: neighbours get the opposite colour, and meeting a neighbour of the same colour closes an odd cycle. Each camper is queued once and each rivalry is examined twice, so the time is O(campers + rivalries). Memory is O(campers + rivalries) for the adjacency lists plus the colour array and queue. Union-find with parity or an iterative DFS are equally valid.

steps.title: Colour from camper 0
steps.content: On the loop 0-1-2-3-0, camper 0 gets cabin 0, then 1 and 3 get cabin 1, then 2 gets cabin 0.

steps.title: Check the closing edge
steps.content: When 2 looks at 3 and 3 looks at 0 the cabins differ, so there is no clash and the answer is true.

steps.title: Odd cycle
steps.content: On the triangle, camper 0 gets cabin 0 and campers 1 and 2 both get cabin 1. When camper 1 examines rival 2, both are in cabin 1, so false is returned.
